title: Sharing policy: per project local only, knowledge only, or knowledge and memory;
input: Sharing policy: per project local only, knowledge only, or knowledge and memory; per knowledge area private or shared; settings in the data directory's env file and in the viewer's Settings; one predicate every sync reads so what is private never reaches the server; ADR 0025.

`setLevel` refuses a project without a `remote:` alias (`no-remote`), a disabled project (`disabled`), an unknown project (`no-project`), an unknown level (`invalid`) and a widening without `confirm` (`needs-confirm`), reading the stored row and the project's state inside its transaction so a stale caller is still refused; `previewLevel` reports `widened` true from `local` to `knowledge` and from `knowledge` to `all`, false the other way; the same effective level twice writes and logs nothing, except a row whose alias is gone, which is rebound and logged; `local` deletes the row and answers an empty `boundAlias`; `applySettingsPatch` refuses a widening without `confirm`, writes the file, logs `roots` or `areas`, adds one to the counter once and sets the baseline to the file's lists in one transaction, and with a file write that throws leaves no row, no counter change and the file as it was; `previewSettingsPatch` compares against the file's lists; `reconcileSettings` reads the file and the baseline inside its transaction, logs a hand edit with source `file`, adds one to the counter and clears the problem, treats a missing baseline as empty lists, does nothing when the lists match, and logs nothing when two processes with different environments look at one file and one baseline; `reconcileLevels` reads the rows and the projects inside its transaction, removes a row whose downgrade still holds, keeps one set again meanwhile, logs with source `system` and adds one to the counter; `resetLevels` deletes every row when the table exists, logs one `levels` change with source `restore` when rows were deleted, sets the counter to `max(floor, copy) + 1`, renews the generation, sets the baseline to the lists given, returns the count, and runs on a copy without the sharing tables.; `setLevel` binds only a host-led remote alias (one whose normalized remote starts with a host name, as `github.com/x/y` does), so a project whose remotes are all local paths or `file://` URLs is refused with `no-remote` and no row is written, and for a project with a host-led remote beside a path remote the bound alias is the host-led one

decisions.question: Where does a project's sharing level live: a column on the projects table (edited in the viewer's project rows and by the CLI), or a comma list in the env file?
decisions.default: A column on projects (core migration 8), local by default; the env file keeps the two workspace-level keys (the workspace switch and the shared areas). The project list lives in the database and the viewer edits rows; a list of project keys in one env line would not scale and could not be edited per row.
decisions.answer: A column on projects (core migration 8), local by default; the env file keeps the two workspace-level keys (the workspace switch and the shared areas). The project list lives in the database and the viewer edits rows; a list of project keys in one env line would not scale and could not be edited per row.

decisions.question: What are the defaults: every project local, the workspace knowledge off and no shared area (nothing leaves until the person chooses), or something shared by default once a team exists?
decisions.default: Everything local: every project local, the workspace switch off, the shared-areas list empty. Nothing leaves the machine until the person chooses, project by project and area by area.
decisions.answer: Everything local: every project local, the workspace switch off, the shared-areas list empty. Nothing leaves the machine until the person chooses, project by project and area by area.

decisions.question: Is the area policy a list of shared areas (private by default) or a list of private areas (shared by default)?
decisions.default: A list of shared areas: an area leaves only when named. Private by default is the deny side, and a new area added later is private until the person shares it.
decisions.answer: A list of shared areas: an area leaves only when named. Private by default is the deny side, and a new area added later is private until the person shares it.

decisions.question: Do the author's own rules (user memories, ADR 0018) ever leave the machine in this part?
decisions.default: Never in this part: a user rule is personal, kept with a project only as provenance; a later part may offer to share them. A memory leaves only when its project is set to all and it is not a user rule.

decisions.question: Is the shared scope repository (the team's) subject to the area list too, or does everything in it leave?
decisions.default: Subject to the area list too: an entry in a private area never leaves, even from the shared repository. The person's choice of what is private holds everywhere; a later part may let the team's taxonomy say otherwise.
decisions.answer: Subject to the area list too: an entry in a private area never leaves, even from the shared repository. The person's choice of what is private holds everywhere; a later part may let the team's taxonomy say otherwise.

decisions.question: Which memories leave when a project is set to all: every active memory of the project that is not a user rule, or only memories above an importance?
decisions.default: Every active memory of the project that is not a user rule; archived and superseded memories never. The level is the person's choice for the whole project; an importance filter is a later refinement if the team asks.
decisions.answer: Every active memory of the project that is not a user rule; archived and superseded memories never. The level is the person's choice for the whole project; an importance filter is a later refinement if the team asks.

decisions.question: Where does the person set the per-project level in the viewer: a selector in each row of the Across projects view (with the workspace switch and the areas in a Settings card), or everything in Settings?
decisions.default: A selector in each project's row of the Across projects view, and a Sharing card in Settings for the workspace switch and the areas. The project list is already in that view; a Settings card cannot list ninety projects well.

decisions.question: Where do the per-project levels live: a column on projects by core migration 8, or tables in a sharing namespace of module_migrations so that user_version stays 7 and 0.6.0 still opens the database?

This keeps the rollback to 0.6.0 that parts 1 and 2 promised and avoids rebuilding projects to widen a CHECK.

decisions.question: Is a project's level one value, or one value per destination (server), so that a second team configured later never inherits what was allowed for the first?
decisions.default: One value per (project, destination). This part has one destination, named team, which the team server part binds to the one server the mission describes; a second destination starts with every level local; the predicate takes the destination as an argument and answers keep for an unknown one.

decisions.question: What leaves the machine for an allowed entry: the exported current content of that one entry, or the knowledge repository (a git push, carrying history, proposals and past versions)?
decisions.default: The exported current content of one allowed item, never a repository: git history, proposals, drafts and archived entries never leave; the sync reads the bytes it sends after ensureFresh and a clean git status, never a stale index row. This is the rule the team server and the sync parts build against.

decisions.question: Does the predicate answer yes or no, or send, withdraw or keep with a reason, and does this part create the ledger of what left?
decisions.default: Send, withdraw or keep, with a reason code and the policy epoch, reading the ledger record the caller passes for the item. The table sharing_ledger (destination, item kind, item uid, direction, version, hash, epoch, times) is created here and written by the server and sync parts; an item received from a destination is never sent to another and never back. A memory's uid is its row id on this machine (memories are never deleted); an entry's is its UUID.

decisions.question: Is the area list one flat set of ids over both taxonomies, with the shared repository always shared, or are ids root-qualified with the roots that may leave named in their own list?
decisions.default: Root-qualified ids (workspace:sales, shared:sales) in the areas key, the workspace's ids governing the workspace and every project repository; and a list of roots that may leave in a roots key (the two settings keys are named in the spec), default empty, so the shared repository leaves only when named, like the workspace. The area rule of D-5 stands; its always clause is superseded.

decisions.question: Do the two sharing keys follow the settings rule that the environment wins over the file, or can the environment only narrow what the file allows?
decisions.default: The file is the policy; an environment value is honoured only when it narrows (an empty or shorter list), a widening value is ignored and doctor warns about it. A stray variable in a shell profile or a host's env block must never share from one process only.

decisions.question: How does the policy load when something is wrong: a hand-edited value that does not parse, a missing table, an unreadable file, an area id that is in no taxonomy?
decisions.default: Fail closed: any failure to load gives a policy where nothing leaves, logged once; one invalid token empties the whole area list and doctor names it; an id not in its root's current taxonomy is inert (never shared) and the viewer's next save drops it; both lists are parsed trimmed, lower-cased and de-duplicated, every token checked.

decisions.question: Which memories leave at the level all, given that memories carry stale, scope (project or branch) and origin (distilled, manual, imported) besides status and the user-rule mark?
decisions.default: Exactly: status active, stale 0, scope project, origin not imported, and not one of the author's rules. The set is fixed in ADR 0025; a level with a different set is a new level name, so what left under all is never reinterpreted. Supersedes D-6's every active memory.

decisions.question: What ties a level to a project's identity, so that adoption of an imported project, a reused folder, a remapped knowledge repository, a disabled project or a restored backup never hands a level to data the person did not choose?
decisions.default: A level above local needs the project's remote alias and is bound to it; when the project no longer carries that alias the predicate answers local and doctor warns. A disabled project, a repository mapped to project 0, an orphan folder and an ambiguous manifest answer local. Restore resets every level to local and logs it; move keeps them. A folder reused by a repository without a remote keeps the old project id today, which the ADR names as a limit.

decisions.question: Is a change of level, roots or areas recorded and confirmed, given that every host gives agents a shell and a widening is a privacy decision?
decisions.default: Every change is recorded in a change log with its time, old value, new value and source (viewer, CLI, restore); a policy epoch in meta grows on every change, the predicate returns it, the ledger records it, and the sync re-reads the policy at every batch and stops when the epoch moved. A widening asks for confirmation: the viewer shows the counts it releases, the CLI asks on a TTY or needs --yes. The boundary stays part 1's: an agent with a shell can still do it, and the log is how a person finds out.

Product text carries no part numbers. Across projects shows each row's level and the project dock sets it with the confirmation. Supersedes D-7's separate card.

decisions.question: Which metadata accompanies an allowed item, what never leaves whatever the policy says, and is redaction at the edge part of the predicate's contract?
decisions.default: With an allowed entry: its current frontmatter and body, its scope and its project's remote alias. With an allowed memory: redacted title and body, kind, importance, status, created and updated times, the project's remote alias. Never: turns, sessions, the history index, hook runs, injections, memory file paths, search terms, branch, commit sha, transcript paths, local path and gitdir aliases, the project key, commit e-mails. Every text that leaves passes redact at the edge, which keeps the private-block promise; it is a required step of the contract the server and sync parts implement.

decisions.question: Which read-outs of the policy ship, and what does doctor warn about, given that nothing consumes the policy yet?
decisions.default: A sharing line in status for the current project (its level, the roots, the shared areas, the entries and memories of this project that would leave); the viewer's counts through one GET route; one CLI, share, with project <level> [--yes], roots <list>, areas <list>, status [--list] (the items, not only counts) and explain <scope>/<slug> | memory <id> (the predicate's reason). Counts come from the knowledge index after ensureFresh and from memories by its existing index, never on the hook path. doctor is ok with the policy's summary and warns only for an invalid raw value, an ignored environment value, a level whose alias the project lost, and an inert area id; sharing configured but no team is not a warning.
decisions.answer: A sharing line in status for the current project (its level, the roots, the shared areas, the entries and memories of this project that would leave); the viewer's counts through one GET route; one CLI, share, with project <level> [--yes], roots <list>, areas <list>, status [--list] (the items, not only counts) and explain <scope>/<slug> | memory <id> (the predicate's reason). Counts come from the knowledge index after ensureFresh and from memories by its existing index, never on the hook path. doctor is ok with the policy's summary and warns only for an invalid raw value, an ignored environment value, a level whose alias the project lost, and an inert area id; sharing configured but no team is not a warning.

decisions.question: The frontend lead's delivery validation (conclave/lead-frontend.delivery.md, R-1 to R-5) asks what this item's UI evidence covers. The captures under review/ui/ are the session's (the standing e2e decision: the viewer's UI evidence is the session's captures), at one desktop width, 1512, in the dark scheme; the spec names no viewport, scheme or motion line; the sub-second loading and saving states and the Backups restore toast with sharingReset above 0 are not captured. Does this item's evidence stop there, with the light scheme, narrower viewports and the three uncaptured states carried to the viewer item (part 3) as advisories, or are those captured by hand now, before the delivery?
decisions.default: It stops there. The spec's state list gains the viewport (1512, the viewer's desktop width), the scheme (dark; the frame is dark in both themes) and the motion thesis (none: no animation added) for this item's pages. The light scheme, narrower viewports, the loading and saving states and the restore toast are carried to the viewer item as advisories, and review/ui-evidence.json is not produced, since the engine writes it only from an e2e run the standing decision does not have.
decisions.answer: 1 (a evidência fica como está: as capturas da sessão a 1512 em tema escuro; tema claro, larguras estreitas e os três estados por capturar vão como avisos para o item do viewer)
